target_customer: Pharmaceutical partners and generic drug makers (first target: children's allergy medication such as loratadine delivered by skin patch)
problem: Children and older adults struggle to swallow pills; passive skin patches could deliver generic drugs but most molecules cannot cross the skin without needles or heat.
business_model: Drug delivery platform technology: develop patch formulations and partner or license with pharmaceutical companies (Bayer accelerator pilot)

founders.name: Shakir Lakhani
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2018-02-19) says he has seasonal and food allergies, which motivated the first product. Education and prior employers not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Keean Sarani
education: University of Waterloo, Honours Science (2016 profile)
founders.background_notes: Ismaili Mail (2016-09-24) says he held conditional admission to pharmacy and had worked in healthcare settings from hospitals to retail pharmacies, and called him CEO at that time; later profiles list Lakhani as CEO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Passive skin delivery of drugs that normally cannot cross the skin requires new materials chemistry (ionic liquids, proline based formulations) and FDA or Health Canada approval via clinical trials.

defensibility.rationale: Two US patents (US 10,576,043 granted 2020-03-03 and US 11,324,705 granted 2022-05-10) name Avro and its founders, and approval pathways take years.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Avro; it worked with Bayer through an accelerator in Toronto from 2018.

market_need_then: Allergy sufferers and caregivers of children wanted alternatives to pills; TechCrunch (2018-02-19) framed the patch as like nicotine patches for children's allergy drugs with possible use for patients who cannot swallow.

identity.visual_style: Clinical biotech site with platform and pipeline pages
identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific, tagline 'Building the future of medical dermatology'

brand_strength.rationale: Press is limited to TechCrunch coverage and accelerator listings; the name shares its spelling with Avro, an aircraft maker, though no source says this mattered.

pivots.why: Founders considered a daily multivitamin patch first; the allergy idea came from seasonal allergy symptoms (profile search result, not opened)

outcome_analysis: Avro began as a University of Waterloo student project in 2016 and raised a roughly $2.2M seed in mid 2018 led by Fifty Years. It then pursued patents, Bayer's accelerator and a pipeline of patch products, and its site now calls it a clinical stage company. No exit or shutdown is reported, but no later financing is documented, so progress after 2022 is unclear.
notes: Aggregators disagree on total raised ($120K Seedtable, $150K CB Insights, $250K Startup Seeker, $2.2M Tryfundable and Parsers); the TechCrunch June 2018 figure of about $2.2M matches the last two and is recorded. Lakhani education was not confirmed by an opened source and is left empty. The company site names Bayer, Thiel Fellowship, Creative Destruction Lab and Velocity as supporters without amounts. Stage is described as pre clinical by some sources and clinical stage by others.
